sanskrit: dhundhumāraś ca rājarṣiḥ satreṣv eva jarāṃ gataḥ prītidāyaṃ parityajya suṣvāpa sa girivraje
english: And the royal sage Dhundhumāra grew old amid his very sacrifices; abandoning the gifts of his affection, he slept on at Girivraja.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrair mahābalaiḥ punaḥ pratyāhṛtaṃ caiva na daivād bhujasaṃśrayāt
english: The kingdom of the Pāṇḍavas was wrested away by the mighty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and won back again — not by fate, but by the strength of their own arms.

sanskrit: taponiyamasaṃyuktā munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ kiṃ te daivabalāc chāpam utsṛjante na karmaṇā
english: The sages, devoted to austerity and self-restraint, firm in their vows — do they hurl their curses by the power of fate, or rather by their own deeds?

sanskrit: pāpam utsṛjate loke sarvaṃ prāpya sudurlabham lobhamohasamāpannaṃ na daivaṃ trāyate naram
english: A man may attain in this world all that is most hard to win, yet cast it away through sin; once fallen into greed and delusion, fate cannot save him.

sanskrit: yathāgniḥ pavanoddhūtaḥ sūkṣmo 'pi bhavate mahān tathā karmasamāyuktaṃ daivaṃ sādhu vivardhate
english: As fire, though small, when fanned by the wind grows great, so fate, when joined to action, prospers and increases well.

sanskrit: yathā tailakṣayād dīpaḥ pramlānim upagacchati tathā karmakṣayād daivaṃ pramlānim upagacchati
english: As a lamp, when its oil is spent, fades and dies away, so fate, when one's works are exhausted, fades and dies away.

sanskrit: vipulam api dhanaughaṃ prāpya bhogān striyo vā; puruṣa iha na śaktaḥ karmahīno 'pi bhoktum sunihitam api cārthaṃ daivatai rakṣyamāṇaṃ; vyayaguṇam api sādhuṃ karmaṇā saṃśrayante
english: Though a man here win a vast flood of wealth, enjoyments, and women, if he is bereft of action he has not the power to enjoy them; and even riches well-secured and guarded by the gods, ample and ready to be spent, men gain hold of only through their own deeds.

sanskrit: bhavati manujalokād devaloko viśiṣṭo; bahutarasusamṛddhyā mānuṣāṇāṃ gṛhāṇi pitṛvanabhavanābhaṃ dṛśyate cāmarāṇāṃ; na ca phalati vikarmā jīvalokena daivam
english: The world of the gods surpasses the world of men by its far greater abundance; beside the dwellings of the immortals, the houses of mortals seem like haunts of the burial-ground — yet for the man of evil deeds fate bears no fruit in the world of the living.

sanskrit: vyapanayati vimārgaṃ nāsti daive prabhutvaṃ; gurum iva kṛtam agryaṃ karma saṃyāti daivam anupahatam adīnaṃ kāmakāreṇa daivaṃ; nayati puruṣakāraḥ saṃcitas tatra tatra
english: Human effort leads astray a man who goes the wrong path — fate has no sovereign power; like a weighty teacher, foremost action carries fate along. Unharmed and unbowed, fate is steered at will by accumulated human effort, here and everywhere.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ mayā vai munisattama phalaṃ puruṣakārasya sadā saṃdṛśya tattvataḥ
english: All this I have now declared to you, O best of sages — the fruit of human effort, ever beheld and known in its truth.

sanskrit: abhyutthānena daivasya samārabdhena karmaṇā vidhinā karmaṇā caiva svargamārgam avāpnuyāt
english: By rousing fate through action duly undertaken, and by deeds performed according to the ordinance, a man may attain the road to heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca karmaṇāṃ me samastānāṃ śubhānāṃ bharatarṣabha phalāni mahatāṃ śreṣṭha prabrūhi paripṛcchataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O bull of the Bhāratas, of all good deeds, O foremost of the great, declare to me, who ask of you, their fruits.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rahasyaṃ yad ṛṣīṇāṃ tu tac chṛṇuṣva yudhiṣṭhira yā gatiḥ prāpyate yena pretyabhāve cirepsitā
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, Yudhiṣṭhira, the secret of the seers — by what means is attained, in the life after death, the long-desired goal.

sanskrit: yena yena śarīreṇa yad yat karma karoti yaḥ tena tena śarīreṇa tat tat phalam upāśnute
english: With whatever body a man performs whatever deed, with that same body he enjoys its several fruits.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ yasyām avasthāyāṃ yat karoti śubhāśubham tasyāṃ tasyām avasthāyāṃ bhuṅkte janmani janmani
english: In whatever state a man does good or evil, in that same state he tastes it, birth after birth.

sanskrit: na naśyati kṛtaṃ karma sadā pañcendriyair iha te hy asya sākṣiṇo nityaṃ ṣaṣṭha ātmā tathaiva ca
english: The deed once done is never lost; here the five senses are ever its witnesses, and the self is the sixth, likewise eternal.

sanskrit: cakṣur dadyān mano dadyād vācaṃ dadyāc ca sūnṛtām anuvrajed upāsīta sa yajñaḥ pañcadakṣiṇaḥ
english: Let a man give his eye, give his mind, and give kindly truthful speech; let him walk behind his guest and wait upon him — that is a sacrifice with fivefold offering.

sanskrit: yo dadyād aparikliṣṭam annam adhvani vartate śrāntāyādṛṣṭapūrvāya tasya puṇyaphalaṃ mahat
english: He who, without grudging, gives food upon the road to a weary stranger never seen before — great is the fruit of his merit.

sanskrit: sthaṇḍile śayamānānāṃ gṛhāṇi śayanāni ca cīravalkalasaṃvīte vāsāṃsy ābharaṇāni ca
english: For those who lie upon the bare ground there shall be houses and couches; for those clad in rags and bark-cloth, garments and ornaments.

sanskrit: vāhanāsanayānāni yogātmani tapodhane agnīn upaśayānasya rājapauruṣam ucyate
english: For the man of disciplined soul, rich in austerity, who sleeps beside his sacred fires, there shall be mounts, seats, and chariots, and the estate of royalty, it is said.

sanskrit: rasānāṃ pratisaṃhāre saubhāgyam anugacchati āmiṣapratisaṃhāre paśūn putrāṃś ca vindati
english: From the renouncing of savory tastes good fortune follows; from the renouncing of meat a man gains cattle and sons.

sanskrit: avākśirās tu yo lambed udavāsaṃ ca yo vaset satataṃ caikaśāyī yaḥ sa labhetepsitāṃ gatim
english: He who hangs head downward, who dwells immersed in water, and who ever sleeps alone — he shall attain the goal of his desire.

sanskrit: pādyam āsanam evātha dīpam annaṃ pratiśrayam dadyād atithipūjārthaṃ sa yajñaḥ pañcadakṣiṇaḥ
english: Water for the feet, a seat, a lamp, food, and shelter — let him give these in honor of his guest: that too is a sacrifice with fivefold offering.

sanskrit: vīrāsanaṃ vīraśayyāṃ vīrasthānam upāsataḥ akṣayās tasya vai lokāḥ sarvakāmagamās tathā
english: For him who keeps the hero's posture, the hero's bed, and the hero's station, the worlds are imperishable and lead to every desire fulfilled.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ labheta dānena maunenājñāṃ viśāṃ pate upabhogāṃś ca tapasā brahmacaryeṇa jīvitam
english: By giving a man wins wealth, by silence command, O lord of peoples; by austerity enjoyments, and by chastity long life.

sanskrit: rūpam aiśvaryam ārogyam ahiṃsāphalam aśnute phalamūlāśināṃ rājyaṃ svargaḥ parṇāśināṃ tathā
english: Beauty, sovereignty, and health are the fruit that non-violence brings; for those who eat fruits and roots, a kingdom; and heaven for those who eat but leaves.

sanskrit: prāyopaveśanād rājyaṃ sarvatra sukham ucyate svargaṃ satyena labhate dīkṣayā kulam uttamam
english: From fasting unto death comes a kingdom, and happiness everywhere, it is said; by truth a man wins heaven, and by consecration a noble birth.

sanskrit: gavāḍhyaḥ śākadīkṣāyāṃ svargagāmī tṛṇāśanaḥ striyas triṣavaṇaṃ snātvā vāyuṃ pītvā kratuṃ labhet
english: By the vow of eating only herbs a man becomes rich in cattle; eating only grass, he goes to heaven. Women who bathe at the three pressings and drink only the wind win the merit of a sacrifice.

sanskrit: salilāśī bhaved yaś ca sadāgniḥ saṃskṛto dvijaḥ maruṃ sādhayato rājyaṃ nākapṛṣṭham anāśake
english: The twice-born who lives on water alone, ever tending his sacred fire and duly consecrated, who masters the desert wilderness, gains a kingdom; and by total fasting, the summit of heaven.

sanskrit: upavāsaṃ ca dīkṣāṃ ca abhiṣekaṃ ca pārthiva kṛtvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi vīrasthānād viśiṣyate
english: He who keeps fasting, consecration, and the ritual bathing, O king, for twelve years, surpasses even the reward of the hero's station.

sanskrit: adhītya sarvavedān vai sadyo duḥkhāt pramucyate mānasaṃ hi caran dharmaṃ svargalokam avāpnuyāt
english: Having studied all the Vedas, a man is at once released from sorrow; practicing the dharma of the mind, he attains the world of heaven.

sanskrit: yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryataḥ yo 'sau prāṇāntiko rogas tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham
english: That craving which the foolish cannot abandon, which does not age though the man ages, that disease which lasts until the breath departs — happy is he who casts it off.

sanskrit: yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram evaṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ karma kartāram anugacchati
english: As among a thousand cows the calf finds its own mother, so the deed once done in the past follows after its doer.

sanskrit: acodyamānāni yathā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca svakālaṃ nātivartante tathā karma purākṛtam
english: As flowers and fruits, unbidden, do not pass beyond their season, so the deed done in the past comes at its appointed time.

sanskrit: jīryanti jīryataḥ keśā dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ cakṣuḥśrotre ca jīryete tṛṣṇaikā tu na jīryate
english: As a man grows old, his hair grows old; his teeth grow old as he grows old; his eyes and ears grow old — yet craving alone never grows old.

sanskrit: yena prīṇāti pitaraṃ tena prītaḥ prajāpatiḥ prīṇāti mātaraṃ yena pṛthivī tena pūjitā yena prīṇāty upādhyāyaṃ tena syād brahma pūjitam
english: By that whereby he pleases his father, Prajāpati is pleased; by that whereby he pleases his mother, the Earth is honored; by that whereby he pleases his teacher, the Brahman itself is worshipped.

sanskrit: sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ anādṛtās tu yasyaite sarvās tasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ
english: He who honors these three has honored all his duties; but he who honors them not — all his rites are without fruit.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhīṣmasya tad vacaḥ śrutvā vismitāḥ kurupuṃgavāḥ āsan prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ prītimanto 'bhavaṃs tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those words of Bhīṣma, the bulls of the Kurus were filled with wonder, their hearts gladdened, and they were then well content.

sanskrit: yan mantre bhavati vṛthā prayujyamāne; yat some bhavati vṛthābhiṣūyamāṇe yac cāgnau bhavati vṛthābhihūyamāne; tat sarvaṃ bhavati vṛthābhidhīyamāne
english: What is lost when the sacred verse is uttered in vain, what is lost when the Soma is pressed in vain, what is lost when the oblation is poured into the fire in vain — all that is lost when speech itself is spoken in vain.

sanskrit: ity etad ṛṣiṇā proktam uktavān asmi yad vibho śubhāśubhaphalaprāptau kim ataḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Thus what was declared by the seer I have now told, O mighty one, concerning the gaining of the fruits of good and evil. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ke pūjyāḥ ke namaskāryāḥ kān namasyasi bhārata etan me sarvam ācakṣva yeṣāṃ spṛhayase nṛpa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who are to be worshipped, who are to be saluted, to whom do you bow, O Bhārata? Tell me all this, O king — those for whom you yearn.

sanskrit: uttamāpadgatasyāpi yatra te vartate manaḥ manuṣyaloke sarvasmin yad amutreha cāpy uta
english: Even in the midst of the gravest peril, where your mind ever turns — in all this world of men, and there beyond as well as here.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca spṛhayāmi dvijātīnāṃ yeṣāṃ brahma paraṃ dhanam yeṣāṃ svapratyayaḥ svargas tapaḥsvādhyāyasādhanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: I yearn for those twice-born ones whose highest wealth is the sacred Brahman, whose heaven rests on their own faith, won by austerity and the study of scripture.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ vṛddhāś ca bālāś ca pitṛpaitāmahīṃ dhuram udvahanti na sīdanti teṣāṃ vai spṛhayāmy aham
english: Those whose elders and whose young alike bear up the yoke of their fathers and forefathers and do not falter — for them indeed I yearn.

sanskrit: vidyāsv abhivinītānāṃ dāntānāṃ mṛdubhāṣiṇām śrutavṛttopapannānāṃ sadākṣaravidāṃ satām
english: Of those well-trained in the branches of knowledge, self-controlled, gentle of speech, endowed with learning and good conduct, ever knowing the sacred syllable, the virtuous —

sanskrit: saṃsatsu vadatāṃ yeṣāṃ haṃsānām iva saṃghaśaḥ maṅgalyarūpā rucirā divyajīmūtaniḥsvanāḥ
english: As they speak in the assemblies, their voices, like the gathered calls of swans, are auspicious in form, lovely, and resonant as the celestial thunderclouds —

sanskrit: samyag uccāritā vācaḥ śrūyante hi yudhiṣṭhira śuśrūṣamāṇe nṛpatau pretya ceha sukhāvahāḥ
english: Their well-uttered words are heard, O Yudhiṣṭhira, by the attentive king, bringing happiness both here and in the world hereafter.

sanskrit: ye cāpi teṣāṃ śrotāraḥ sadā sadasi saṃmatāḥ vijñānaguṇasaṃpannās teṣāṃ ca spṛhayāmy aham
english: And those who are their listeners, ever honored in the assembly, endowed with the virtue of discernment — for them too I yearn.

sanskrit: susaṃskṛtāni prayatāḥ śucīni guṇavanti ca dadaty annāni tṛptyarthaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo yudhiṣṭhira ye cāpi satataṃ rājaṃs teṣāṃ ca spṛhayāmy aham
english: Those who, pure and diligent, give well-prepared, clean, and wholesome food to the brāhmaṇas for their full satisfaction, O Yudhiṣṭhira — and who do so unceasingly, O king — for them too I yearn.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ hy evāhave yoddhuṃ na dātum anasūyitam śūrā vīrāś ca śataśaḥ santi loke yudhiṣṭhira teṣāṃ saṃkhyāyamānānāṃ dānaśūro viśiṣyate
english: It is possible to fight in battle, but not to give without grudging; the brave and valiant exist by the hundreds in this world, Yudhiṣṭhira; but among them all, when they are counted, the hero of giving stands supreme.

sanskrit: dhanyaḥ syāṃ yady ahaṃ bhūyaḥ saumya brāhmaṇako 'pi vā kule jāto dharmagatis tapovidyāparāyaṇaḥ
english: Blessed should I be, O gentle one, were I born again even as a humble brāhmaṇa, sprung from a noble line, set upon the path of dharma, devoted to austerity and learning.

sanskrit: na me tvattaḥ priyataro loke 'smin pāṇḍunandana tvattaś ca me priyatarā brāhmaṇā bharatarṣabha
english: There is none in this world dearer to me than you, O joy of Pāṇḍu; yet dearer to me than you are the brāhmaṇas, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yathā mama priyatarās tvatto viprāḥ kurūdvaha tena satyena gaccheyaṃ lokān yatra sa śaṃtanuḥ
english: As the brāhmaṇas are dearer to me than you, O foremost of the Kurus — by that truth may I go to those worlds where Śaṃtanu dwells.

sanskrit: na me pitā priyataro brāhmaṇebhyas tathābhavat na me pituḥ pitā vāpi ye cānye 'pi suhṛjjanāḥ
english: Not my own father was dearer to me than the brāhmaṇas, nor my father's father, nor any of my other kinsmen and friends.

sanskrit: na hi me vṛjinaṃ kiṃ cid vidyate brāhmaṇeṣv iha aṇu vā yadi vā sthūlaṃ viditaṃ sādhukarmabhiḥ
english: For no offense of mine against the brāhmaṇas is known here, be it small or great — as is known to those of righteous deeds.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vāpi vācā vāpi paraṃtapa yan me kṛtaṃ brāhmaṇeṣu tenādya na tapāmy aham
english: By deed, by thought, or by word, O scorcher of foes, whatever I have done toward the brāhmaṇas — for that I feel no torment today.

sanskrit: brahmaṇya iti mām āhus tayā vācāsmi toṣitaḥ etad eva pavitrebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ paramaṃ smṛtam
english: "Devoted to the brāhmaṇas" — so they call me, and by those words I am made content; this very thing is held the highest of all things that purify.

sanskrit: paśyāmi lokān amalāñ chucīn brāhmaṇayāyinaḥ teṣu me tāta gantavyam ahnāya ca cirāya ca
english: I behold the stainless, pure worlds attained by those devoted to the brāhmaṇas; thither, my son, must I go, whether soon or after long.

sanskrit: yathā patyāśrayo dharmaḥ strīṇāṃ loke yudhiṣṭhira sa devaḥ sā gatir nānyā kṣatriyasya tathā dvijāḥ
english: As the dharma of women in the world rests upon the husband, O Yudhiṣṭhira — he their god, he their refuge, and no other — so for the kṣatriya are the twice-born.

sanskrit: kṣatriyaḥ śatavarṣī ca daśavarṣī ca brāhmaṇaḥ pitāputrau ca vijñeyau tayor hi brāhmaṇaḥ pitā
english: A kṣatriya of a hundred years and a brāhmaṇa of ten are to be regarded as father and son — and of the two, the brāhmaṇa is the father.

sanskrit: nārī tu patyabhāve vai devaraṃ kurute patim pṛthivī brāhmaṇālābhe kṣatriyaṃ kurute patim
english: As a woman, in the absence of a husband, takes her husband's brother for husband, so the Earth, lacking a brāhmaṇa, takes the kṣatriya for her lord.

sanskrit: putravac ca tato rakṣyā upāsyā guruvac ca te agnivac copacaryā vai brāhmaṇāḥ kurusattama
english: And so the brāhmaṇas are to be protected as one's sons, waited upon as one's teachers, and tended as the sacred fire, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: ṛjūn sataḥ satyaśīlān sarvabhūtahite ratān āśīviṣān iva kruddhān dvijān upacaret sadā
english: Upright, virtuous, true in their conduct, devoted to the good of all beings — yet, when angered, like venomous serpents — such twice-born ones a man should ever serve with care.

sanskrit: tejasas tapasaś caiva nityaṃ bibhyed yudhiṣṭhira ubhe caite parityājye tejaś caiva tapas tathā
english: One should ever stand in dread of their fiery energy and their austerity, O Yudhiṣṭhira; both of these are to be guarded against — their splendor and likewise their penance.

sanskrit: vyavasāyas tayoḥ śīghram ubhayor eva vidyate hanyuḥ kruddhā mahārāja brāhmaṇā ye tapasvinaḥ
english: In both of these the resolve to act is swift indeed; for when angered, O great king, the brāhmaṇas who are rich in austerity can slay.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ syād ubhayaṃ dattaṃ brāhmaṇād yad akopanāt kuryād ubhayataḥśeṣaṃ dattaśeṣaṃ na śeṣayet
english: Whatever is given to a brāhmaṇa who is free of anger returns in twofold measure; let a man, when giving, keep no remainder back, but give without leaving a remnant on either side.

sanskrit: daṇḍapāṇir yathā goṣu pālo nityaṃ sthiro bhavet brāhmaṇān brahma ca tathā kṣatriyaḥ paripālayet
english: As a herdsman, staff in hand, stands ever steadfast over his cattle, so should the kṣatriya guard the brāhmaṇas and the sacred Brahman.

sanskrit: piteva putrān rakṣethā brāhmaṇān brahmatejasaḥ gṛhe caiṣām avekṣethāḥ kaccid astīha jīvanam
english: As a father guards his sons, so should you guard the brāhmaṇas radiant with the splendor of the Brahman; and look into their households, whether their livelihood holds here.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brāhmaṇānāṃ tu ye loke pratiśrutya pitāmaha na prayacchanti mohāt te ke bhavanti mahāmate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Those in the world who, having promised a gift to the brāhmaṇas, give it not through delusion, O grandsire — what do they become, O most wise?

sanskrit: etan me tattvato brūhi dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara pratiśrutya durātmāno na prayacchanti ye narāḥ
english: Tell me this truly, the law of it, O best of the upholders of dharma — those evil-souled men who, having promised, do not give.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yo na dadyāt pratiśrutya svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu āśās tasya hatāḥ sarvāḥ klībasyeva prajāphalam
english: Bhīṣma said: He who, having promised little or much, does not give — all his hopes are destroyed, like the fruit of offspring in a eunuch.

sanskrit: yāṃ rātriṃ jāyate pāpo yāṃ ca rātriṃ vinaśyati etasminn antare yad yat sukṛtaṃ tasya bhārata yac ca tasya hutaṃ kiṃ cit sarvaṃ tasyopahanyate
english: From the night that wretch is born to the night that he perishes, whatever good he has done in that interval, O Bhārata, and whatever oblation he has offered — all of it is undone.

sanskrit: atraitad vacanaṃ prāhur dharmaśāstravido janāḥ niśamya bharataśreṣṭha buddhyā paramayuktayā
english: On this the people learned in the law-books have spoken this saying — hear it, O best of the Bhāratas, with a mind most attentive.

sanskrit: api codāharantīmaṃ dharmaśāstravido janāḥ aśvānāṃ śyāmakarṇānāṃ sahasreṇa sa mucyate
english: And the people learned in the law-books cite this also: by a thousand horses with dark ears that man is released.

sanskrit: atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam sṛgālasya ca saṃvādaṃ vānarasya ca bhārata
english: On this very matter they relate an ancient tale, the converse of the jackal and the monkey, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tau sakhāyau purā hy āstāṃ mānuṣatve paraṃtapa anyāṃ yoniṃ samāpannau sārgālīṃ vānarīṃ tathā
english: The two had once been friends in their state as men, O scorcher of foes, but had passed into other births — the one a jackal, the other a monkey.

sanskrit: tataḥ parāsūn khādantaṃ sṛgālaṃ vānaro 'bravīt śmaśānamadhye saṃprekṣya pūrvajātim anusmaran
english: Then, seeing the jackal devouring the dead in the midst of the burning-ground, the monkey, recalling their former birth, spoke to him.

sanskrit: kiṃ tvayā pāpakaṃ karma kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ sudāruṇam yas tvaṃ śmaśāne mṛtakān pūtikān atsi kutsitān
english: What grievous and most terrible deed did you commit of old, that here in the burning-ground you eat the rotting, loathsome corpses?

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca sṛgālo vānaraṃ tadā brāhmaṇasya pratiśrutya na mayā tad upākṛtam
english: Thus addressed, the jackal answered the monkey then: "Having made a promise to a brāhmaṇa, I did not fulfill it."

sanskrit: tatkṛte pāpikāṃ yonim āpanno 'smi plavaṃgama tasmād evaṃvidhaṃ bhakṣyaṃ bhakṣayāmi bubhukṣitaḥ
english: "For that I have come into this sinful birth, O leaping one; therefore, hungering, I eat such food as this."
